candidates.label: Ancient Corinth (Archaia Korinthos)
candidates.support: The extensively excavated site at Archaia Korinthos, distinct from the modern city of Corinth a few kilometers away, is undisputed as the location of the ancient and New Testament city; Pleiades and Wikidata's coordinates agree closely.

summary.text: Corinth stood on the narrow isthmus joining central Greece to the Peloponnese, below the steep rock of Acrocorinthus, a citadel hill rising more than 1,800 feet directly south of the city. The Roman general Mummius destroyed the Greek city in 146 BC, and the Roman leader Julius Caesar refounded it as a Roman colony in 44 BC; it grew quickly, and by Paul's time it was the leading city of the Peloponnese. Corinth's twin harbors, Lechaeum on the Corinthian Gulf and Cenchreae on the Saronic Gulf, let traders avoid the long voyage around the Peloponnese by hauling smaller ships overland on a paved track, the diolkos.

history.text: Acts reports that Paul spent eighteen months in Corinth, lodging and working as a tentmaker alongside the Jewish couple Priscilla and Aquila and teaching the word of God there. When the city's Jewish community brought him before the Roman proconsul Gallio, Gallio refused to judge what he called a dispute about Jewish law rather than a crime, and had the accusers driven from his court. The congregation Paul founded there included members with Latin names such as Crispus, Gaius, and Erastus, reflecting the strongly Roman character of Caesar's colony, and Paul later wrote both 1 Corinthians and 2 Corinthians to the church there.

Some years after Paul's visit, in AD 66-67, the emperor Nero tried to cut a ship canal through the isthmus so that vessels could avoid the overland crossing entirely; the project was never finished, and traces of Nero's unfinished canal were still visible before work began on the modern Corinth Canal.

Today the ruins of ancient Corinth, a few kilometers from the modern city of the same name, form an archaeological site first excavated in 1892. Its best-known standing monument is the Temple of Apollo, built in the sixth century BC, of which seven of the original stone columns still stand.

scripture.textWEB: After these things Paul departed from Athens and came to Corinth.

He found a certain Jew named Aquila, a man of Pontus by race, who had recently come from Italy with his wife Priscilla, because Claudius had commanded all the Jews to depart from Rome. He came to them,
and because he practiced the same trade, he lived with them and worked, for by trade they were tent makers.
Crispus, the ruler of the synagogue, believed in the Lord with all his house. Many of the Corinthians, when they heard, believed and were baptized.
He lived there a year and six months, teaching the word of God among them.
But when Gallio was proconsul of Achaia, the Jews with one accord rose up against Paul and brought him before the judgment seat,

But when Paul was about to open his mouth, Gallio said to the Jews, “If indeed it were a matter of wrong or of wicked crime, you Jews, it would be reasonable that I should bear with you; but if they are questions about words and names and your own law, look to it yourselves. For I don’t want to be a judge of these matters.”
Paul, having stayed after this many more days, took his leave of the brothers, and sailed from there for Syria, together with Priscilla and Aquila. He shaved his head in Cenchreae, for he had a vow.
While Apollos was at Corinth, Paul, having passed through the upper country, came to Ephesus and found certain disciples.
to the assembly of God which is at Corinth—those who are sanctified in Christ Jesus, called saints, with all who call on the name of our Lord Jesus Christ in every place, both theirs and ours:
Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus through the will of God, and Timothy our brother, to the assembly of God which is at Corinth, with all the saints who are in the whole of Achaia:
But I call God for a witness to my soul, that to spare you, I didn’t come to Corinth.
For we don’t stretch ourselves too much, as though we didn’t reach to you. For we came even as far as to you with the Good News of Christ,
Erastus remained at Corinth, but I left Trophimus at Miletus sick.
So he drove them from the judgment seat.
